\section{Diagonalisation of the scalar sector}
\label{app:higgs}
The scalar potential $V_{\rm H}$ of eq.~\eqref{eq:Hpot} is  bounded from below
if
\be
  \lambda_1 \geq 0\ ,\quad\lambda_2 \leq 0\ ,\quad\lambda_3\geq 0\ ,\quad
  \alpha_{12}\geq 0\ ,\quad\alpha_{13}\geq 0\quad\text{and}\quad
  \alpha_2-\alpha_3\geq 0\, ,
\label{eq:copos}\ee
where $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha_i  + \alpha_j$, and if one of the following
conditions is realised,
\be
 \Big[ \lambda_{12}\geq 0 \Big] \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 \Big[ \lambda_{12}\leq 0\ ,\quad \lambda_1+\lambda_2\geq 0
      \quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_1^2+4\lambda_2^2+8\lambda_1\lambda_2\leq 0
  \Big]\ ,
\label{eq:cstr2}\ee
with $\lambda_{12} = \lambda_1 + 2 \lambda_2$. Moreover, its minimisation allows
for the reduction of the number of degrees of freedom of the Higgs sector by
three,
\be
  \mu_1^2 = \alpha_{12} \big(\vL^2+\vR^2\big) + k^2 \lambda_1 +
    \frac{\kappa \vL \vR}{\sqrt{2} k} \ ,\qquad
  \mu_2^2 = \alpha_{12} k^2 + \lambda_3 \big(\vL^2+\vR^2\big) \ , \qquad
  \lambda_4 = \lambda_3 - \frac{\kappa k}{\sqrt{2} \vL \vR} \ .
\label{eq:minpot}\ee
Focusing first on the charged scalar sector, the squared mass matrix turns out
to be block diagonal. The $\phi^\pm_1$ and $\chi_L^\pm$ fields therefore mix
independently from the $\phi_2^\pm$ and $\chi_R^\pm$ fields, as shown by
eq.~\eqref{eq:ch_mix}. The corresponding $2\times 2$ blocks of the mass matrix
$({\cal M}^\pm_L)^2$ and $({\cal M}^\pm_R)^2$ are written, respectively, in
the $(\phi_2^\pm, \chi_L^\pm)$ and $(\phi_1^\pm, \chi_R^\pm)$ bases, as
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.4}
\be\bsp
  ({\cal M}^\pm_{L,R})^2 =  \bpm
     -(\alpha_2-\alpha_3)v_{\scriptscriptstyle L,R}^2 -
         \frac{\kappa \vL \vR}{\sqrt{2}k}~~~~~ & 
     (\alpha_2-\alpha_3) k v_{\scriptscriptstyle L,R} +
         \frac{\kappa v_{\scriptscriptstyle R,L}}{\sqrt{2}}\\
     (\alpha_2-\alpha_3) k + \frac{\kappa v_{\scriptscriptstyle R,L}}{\sqrt{2}}&
     -(\alpha_2-\alpha_3)k^2 - \frac{\kappa k v_{\scriptscriptstyle R,L}}
       {\sqrt{2}v_{\scriptscriptstyle L,R}}\epm \ ,
\esp\ee
and are diagonalised by the rotations of eq.~\eqref{eq:ch_mix}. The
corresponding mass eigenvalues $M_{H_1^\pm}$ and $M_{H_2^\pm}$ are
\be
  M_{H_1^\pm} =  \frac{k^2+\vL^2}{2 k \vL} \Big[-2(\alpha_2-\alpha_3) k \vL -
    \sqrt{2} \kappa \vR\Big] \quad\text{and}\quad
  M_{H_2^\pm} =  \frac{k^2+\vR^2}{2 k \vR} \Big[-2(\alpha_2-\alpha_3) k \vR -
    \sqrt{2} \kappa \vL\Big] \ .
\ee
As $\alpha_2-\alpha_3\geq 0$ from eq.~\eqref{eq:copos}, forbidding tachyonic
fields yields $\kappa < 0$. This further implies $\lambda_4 \geq 0$ by virtue of
eq.~\eqref{eq:minpot}. As shown by eq.~\eqref{eq:nh_mix}, the pseudoscalar and
scalar components of the $\phi_1^0$ field do not mix and consist of the
physical $H_1^0$ and $A_1^0$ eigenstates. They are mass-degenerate, with masses
$M_{H_1^0}$ and $M_{A_1^0}$ reading
\be
  M^2_{H_1^0} = M^2_{A_1^0} = -(\alpha_2-\alpha_3) (\vL^2+\vR^2)
    - \frac{\kappa \vL \vR}{\sqrt{2} k} + 2 k^2 \lambda_2 \ .
\ee
The squared mass matrices $({\cal M}^0_\Re)^2$ and $({\cal M}^0_\Im)^2$ of the
three remaining scalar and pseudoscalar fields are respectively given, in the
$(\Re\{\phi^0_2\}, \Re\{\chi_L^0\}, \Re\{\chi_R^0\})$ and
$(\Im\{\phi^0_2\}, \Im\{\chi_L^0\}, \Im\{\chi_R^0\})$ bases, by
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\setlength\arraycolsep{5pt}
\be\bsp
  ({\cal M}^0_\Re)^2 =&\ \bpm
    2k^2 \lambda_1 \!-\! \frac{\kappa \vL \vR}{\sqrt{2} k} & 2 \alpha_{12} k \vL
      \!+\! \frac{\kappa \vR}{\sqrt{2}} & 2 \alpha_{12} k \vR \!+\!
      \frac{\kappa \vL}{\sqrt{2}}\\
    2\alpha_{12} k \vL \!+\! \frac{\kappa \vR}{\sqrt{2}} & 2 \lambda_3 \vL^2
      \!-\!\frac{\kappa k\vR}{\sqrt{2} \vL} & 2 \lambda_3\vL\vR\!-\!
      \frac{\kappa k}{\sqrt{2}}\\
    2\alpha_{12} k \vR \!+\! \frac{\kappa \vL}{\sqrt{2}} & 2\lambda_3\vL\vR\!-\!
       \frac{\kappa k}{\sqrt{2}}  & 2 \lambda_3 \vR^2 \!-\!
       \frac{\kappa k \vL}{\sqrt{2} \vR}
  \epm \ , \\
  ({\cal M}^0_\Im)^2 =&\ \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{2}} \bpm
    -\frac{\vL \vR}{k} & \vR & - \vL \\
    \vR & -\frac{k \vR}{\vL} & k\\
    -\vL & k & -\frac{k \vL}{\vR} \epm \ ,
\esp\ee
and are diagonalised by the two $U_{3\times 3}^{\rm H}$ and
$U_{3\times 3}^{\rm A}$ rotation matrices of eq.~\eqref{eq:nh_mix}. These are explicitly 
given by
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.6}
\be\bsp
  U_{3\times 3}^{\rm A} = &\
  \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bpm
    -\frac{k}{\sqrt{k^2+\vR^2}} & \frac{k \vR^2}{\sqrt{\big(k^2+\vR^2\big)
     \big(\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2\big)}} &
       \frac{\vR \vL}{\sqrt{\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2}}\\
     0 & \vL \frac{\sqrt{k^2+\vR^2}}{\sqrt{\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2}} &
      - \frac{k \vR}{\sqrt{\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2}}\\
     \frac{\vR}{\sqrt{\vR^2+k^2}} &
     \frac{k^2 \vR}{\sqrt{\big(k^2+\vR^2\big)
     \big(\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2\big)}} &
      \frac{k \vL}{\sqrt{\vL^2 \vR^2+k^2 \vL^2 + \vR^2k^2}}\epm\ ,\\
  U_{3\times 3}^{\rm H} = &\
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bpm
    \frac{f_0}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1}} &
    \frac{f_2(1+g_0^2) - f_0(1+g_0g_2)}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1 {\cal D}_2}} &
    \frac{\xi (g_2-g_0)}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_2}}\\
    \frac{g_0}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1}} &
    \frac{g_2(1+f_0^2) - g_0(1+f_0f_2)}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1 {\cal D}_2}} &
    \frac{\xi (f_0-f_2)}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_2}}\\
    \frac{1}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1}} &
    \frac{f_0^2 + g_0^2 - f_0f_2 -g_0g_2}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_1 {\cal D}_2}} &
    \frac{\xi (g_0f_2-g_2f_0)}{\sqrt{{\cal D}_2}}\epm \ ,
\esp\ee
and depend on various functions of the Higgs mass eigenvalues $M_{H^0_i}$,
\be\bsp
  f_i = &\ \frac{2 M_{H_i^0}^4 \vL \vR + M_{H_i^0}^2 (\vL^2 + \vR^2)
    (\sqrt{2} k \kappa - 4 \vL \vR \lambda_3) - 2 \sqrt{2} k (\vL^2 - \vR^2)^2
    \lambda_3 \kappa}{\vR \Big[M_{H_i^0}^2 (4 k \vL \vR \alpha_{12} +
    \sqrt{2} \vL^2 \kappa) + 2 \sqrt{2} (k^2 \alpha_{12} + \vL^2
    \lambda_3) (\vR^2 - \vL^2) \kappa\Big]} \ ,\\
  g_i = &\ \frac{\vL}{\vR}\ \frac{M_{H_i^0}^2 (4k \vL \vR \alpha_{12} + \sqrt{2}
    \vR^2 \kappa) + 2 \sqrt{2} (k^2 \alpha_{12} + \vR^2 \lambda_3) (\vL^2 -
    \vR^2) \kappa}{M_{H_i^0}^2 (4 k \vL \vR \alpha_{12} + \sqrt{2} \vL^2 \kappa)
    + 2 \sqrt{2} (k^2 \alpha_{12} + \vL^2 \lambda_3) (\vR^2 - \vL^2)\kappa}\ ,\\
  {\cal D}_1 =&\ 1+f_0^2+g_0^2 \ , \\
  {\cal D}_2 =&\ f_2^2 (1+g_0^2) + (g_0-g_2)^2 - 2 f_0 f_2 (1+g_0g_2) +
    f_0^2 (1+g_2^2) \ ,\\
  \xi = &\ {\rm sgn}\big[ g_0(f_2-f_3) + g_2(f_3-f_0)+g_3(f_0-f_2)\big] \ .
\esp\ee
In our conventions, we trade the $\lambda_1$ free parameter of the scalar
potential for the mass of the lightest Higgs state $H_0^0$ (that can then be set
freely and thus match the SM Higgs boson mass). $\lambda_1$ becomes thus a
dependent parameter,
\be\label{eq:lam1}
  \lambda_1 =  \frac{1}{2 k^3}\ \frac{
    \sqrt{2} k \vL \vR M_{H_0^0}^6 + \mathfrak{a}^{(4)} M_{H_0^0}^4
      - 2\mathfrak{a}^{(2)}M_{H_0^0}^2 - 4\alpha_{12}^2\kappa k^4(\vL^2-\vR^2)^2
  }{
    \sqrt{2} \vL \vR M_{H_0^0}^4
      + (\kappa k-2\sqrt{2}\lambda_3 \vL \vR) (\vL^2+\vR^2)M_{H_0^0}^2 
      - 2\kappa k \lambda_3 (\vL^2-\vR^2)^2
  }\ ,
\ee
and the remaining scalar masses then read
\be
  M^2_{A_2^0} =  - \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{2} k \vL \vR}
    \Big[\vL^2 \vR^2 + k^2(\vL^2+\vR^2)\Big] \qquad\text{and} \qquad
 M_{H_{2,3}^0}^2 = \frac12 \bigg[ \mathfrak{a} \pm
   \sqrt{\mathfrak{a}^2 + 4(\mathfrak{b} + \mathfrak{a} M_{H_0^0}^2) }\bigg] \ .
\ee
with
\be\bsp
  \mathfrak{a}^{(4)} = &\ -2\sqrt{2} k \lambda_3 \vL \vR (\vL^2 + \vR^2) +
     \kappa \Big(\vL^2 \vR^2 + k^2 (\vL^2 + \vR^2)\Big) \ ,\\
  \mathfrak{a}^{(2)} = &\  2\sqrt{2} \alpha_{12}^2 k^3 \vL \vR (\vL^2 + \vR^2) +
     \kappa \Big(\lambda_3 \vL^2 \vR^2 (\vL^2 + \vR^2) + k^2 \big[4 \alpha_{12}
       \vL^2 \vR^2 + \lambda_3 (\vL^2 - \vR^2)^2\big]\Big) \  ,\\
  \mathfrak{a} =&\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} k \vL \vR} \bigg[
    \vL \vR \big(2 \sqrt{2} k^3 \lambda_1 - \kappa \vL \vR\big) +
    k \big(2 \sqrt{2} \lambda_3 \vL \vR -\kappa k\big)\big(\vL^2+\vR^2\big)
  \bigg]  -M_{H_0^0}^2\ , \\
  \mathfrak{b} =&\ \frac{1}{k \vL \vR} \bigg[
    \sqrt{2}\kappa k^2\Big(4 \alpha_{12} \vL^2 \vR^2 +
       \lambda_3 (\vL^2 \!-\! \vR^2)^2 \Big)\\ &\qquad\qquad+
    \Big(4 k^3 (\alpha_{12}^2 \!-\! \lambda_1 \lambda_3) \vL \vR +
       \sqrt{2}\kappa (k^4 \lambda_1 \!+\! \lambda_3 \vL^2 \vR^2)\Big)
       \Big(\vL^2 \!+\! \vR^2\Big) 
     \bigg] \ .
\esp\ee



\section{The fermion sector}
\label{app:ferms}
Fermion mass terms are generated from the Yukawa Lagrangian of
eq.~\eqref{eq:yuk} after the breaking of the $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_{R'}\times
U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry down to electromagnetism,
\be
  \lag_{\rm F}^{\rm mass} =
    -\frac{k}{\sqrt{2}}
      \Big[ \bar e_L {\bf \hat Y}^e e_R + \bar u_L {\bf \hat Y}^u u_R \Big]
    -\frac{\vL}{\sqrt{2}}
      \Big[ \bar d_L {\bf \hat Y}^d d_R + \bar \nu_L {\bf \hat Y}^\nu \nu_R\Big]
    -\frac{\vR}{\sqrt{2}}
      \Big[ \bar d'_R {\bf \hat Y}^{d'} d'_L + \bar n_R {\bf \hat Y}^n n_L \Big]
    + {\rm h.c.} 
\ee
The different mass matrices ${\bf \hat Y}$ can be diagonalised through 12
unitary rotations,
\be\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.}\bsp
  \frac{k}{\sqrt{2}}   {\bf\hat Y}^u
    \to \frac{k}{\sqrt{2}}   V_u {\bf Y}^u U_u^\dag
    =    \bpm M_u&0&0\\0&M_c&0\\0&0&M_t\epm \!,\
& \frac{\vL}{\sqrt{2}} {\bf\hat Y}^d
    \to \frac{\vL}{\sqrt{2}} V_d {\bf Y}^d U_d^\dag
    =    \bpm M_d&0&0\\0&M_s&0\\0&0&M_b\epm \!,\\
  \frac{\vL}{\sqrt{2}} {\bf\hat Y}^\nu
    \to \frac{\vL}{\sqrt{2}} V_\nu {\bf Y}^\nu U_\nu^\dag
    = \bpm M_{\nu_e}&0&0\\0&M_{\nu_\mu}&0\\0&0&M_{\nu_\tau}\epm \! ,\
& \frac{k}{\sqrt{2}}   {\bf\hat Y}^e
    \to \frac{k}{\sqrt{2}} V_e{\bf Y}^e U_e^\dag
    =   \bpm M_e&0&0\\0&M_\mu&0\\0&0&M_\tau\epm \! ,\\
  \frac{\vR}{\sqrt{2}}   {\bf\hat Y}^{d'}
    \to \frac{\vR}{\sqrt{2}} U_{d'}{\bf Y}^{d'} V_{d'}^\dag
    =   \bpm M_{d'}&0&0\\0&M_{s'}&0\\0&0&M_{b'}\epm \! ,\
& \frac{\vR}{\sqrt{2}}   {\bf\hat Y}^n
    \to \frac{\vR}{\sqrt{2}} U_n{\bf Y}^n V_n^\dag
    =   \bpm M_{n_e}&0&0\\0&M_{n_\mu}&0\\0&0&M_{n_\tau}\epm \! ,
\esp\ee
leading to diagonal and real ${\bf Y}$ matrices. These rotations
equivalently correspond to replacing the fermion gauge eigenbasis by the
physical one,
\be\bsp
 &  u_L \to V_u   u_L\ , \quad
    ~d_L \to V_d   d_L\ , \quad
  \nu_L \to V_\nu \nu_L\ , \quad
    e_L \to V_e   e_L\ , \quad
    ~d'_L\to V_{d'}d'_L\ , \quad
    n_L \to V_n   n_L\ , \\
 &  u_R \to U_u   u_R\ , \quad
    d_R \to U_d   d_R\ , \quad
  \!\nu_R \to U_\nu \nu_R\ , \quad
   \!e_R \to U_e   e_R\ , \quad
    d'_R\to U_{d'}d'_R\ , \quad
   \!n_R \to U_n   n_R\ .
\esp\ee
As in the SM, conventionally we  keep the left-handed up-type
quark and charged lepton bases unchanged and absorb the $V_u - V_d$ and $V_\nu
- V_e$ rotations in a redefinition of the down-type quark and neutrino states.
Similarly, the $U_u-U_{d'}$ and $U_n-U_e$ rotations are conveniently absorbed in
a redefinition of the $d'_R$ and $n_L$ bases, the right-handed up-type quark and
charged lepton bases being kept unchanged,
\be\bsp
  d_L \to V_u^\dag V_d d_L \equiv V_{\rm CKM} d_L \ , \quad&
  \nu_L \to V_e^\dag V_\nu \nu_L \equiv V_{\rm PMNS} d_L \ , \\
  d'_R \to U_u^\dag U_{d'} d'_R \equiv V_{\rm CKM'} d'_R\ , \quad&
  n_R \to U_e^\dag U_n n_R \equiv V_{\rm PMNS'} n_R \ .
\esp\ee
Omitting any potential Majorana phase, each of the four CKM/PMNS rotation
matrices can be defined by three mixing angles $\theta_{ij}$ and a Dirac phase
$\delta$.

We collect the properties of the new physics fields and external parameters
associated with our \fr\ implementation of the ALRSM model in
tables~\ref{tab:fields} and \ref{tab:parameters}, where we additionally
include properties useful for the user when running any programme relying on our
implementation.

As can be noticed from the tables, the left-handed and right-handed scotinos are
combined to form a Dirac fermion $n_i$ (with $i=1,2,3$ being a generation index)
and the left-handed and right-handed exotic quarks are combined to form a Dirac
fermion $d'_i$ (with $i=1,2,3$ being again a generation index). Whilst all
fermion masses are free parameters of the model (see also
appendix~\ref{app:ferms}), all boson masses are internal (\ie\ are derived
parameters), with the exception of the SM Higgs boson mass $M_{H_0^0}$ (see
appendix~\ref{app:higgs}) and the $Z$-boson mass. As for the SM implementation
included with \fr, our model defines the electroweak sector following the LEP
scheme that is known to yield the minimal parametric uncertainty in the
predictions. The three electroweak inputs are thus the Fermi coupling $\gF$, the
fine structure constant $\alpha$ and the $Z$-boson mass $M_Z$. The gauge and
scalar sectors are then fully defined by fixing nine parameters, that we choose
to be $v'$, $t_\beta$, $\gR$, $\lambda_2$, $\lambda_3$, $\alpha_1$, $\alpha_2$,
$\alpha_3$ and $\kappa$. We recall that the user must ensure that the conditions
of eqs.~\eqref{eq:copos} and \eqref{eq:cstr2} are satisfied when providing the
numerical values of these parameters, and that $\kappa<0$ to avoid tachyonic
charged Higgs bosons.

All other parameters of the gauge and Higgs sectors are then derived as follows.
The vacuum expectation values $v$, $\vL$, $\vR$ and $k$ are obtained from
$\gF$, $v'$ and $t_\beta$,
\be
  v^2 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\gF} \ ,\qquad
  \vL = v\ \cos\beta\ , \qquad
  k = v\ \sin\beta
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \vR^2 = v'^2-k^2 \ .
\ee
As in the SM the $W$-boson mass is derived from the electroweak
inputs,
\be
  M_W^2 = \frac{M_Z^2}{2}
    \bigg[1 + \sqrt{1 - 2\sqrt{2}\frac{\pi\alpha}{\gF M_Z^2}}\bigg] \ ,
\ee
so that eq.~\eqref{eq:mw_mwp} can be used to derive the $SU(2)_L$ gauge
coupling $\gL$. As $e = \sqrt{4 \pi\alpha}$, one can then derive the hypercharge
coupling $\gY$ and the sine and cosine of the electroweak mixing angle $\tw$
from eq.~\eqref{eq:ewmix}, which further allows us to calculate the $B-L$ coupling
constant $\gBL$, the cosine of the $\phw$ mixing angle and the so far neglected
$Z-Z'$ mixing. It is up to the user to verify that his/her choice of input
parameter yields $\tan(2\zw) \lesssim 10^{-3}$. Furthermore, the $W'$- and $Z'$-boson masses are obtained from eqs.~\eqref{eq:mw_mwp} and \eqref{eq:mz_mzp},
and the other parameters of the Higgs potential (\ie, $\mu_1$,
$\mu_2$, $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_4$) are obtained from eq.~\eqref{eq:minpot}
and eq.~\eqref{eq:lam1}.

In the fermion sector, the various CKM and PNMS matrices are obtained from their
standard expressions in terms of three mixing angles and a phase,
\be\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.}
  V = \bpm
   c_{12} c_{13} & s_{12}c_{13}& s_{13}e^{-i\delta}\\
   -s_{12}c_{23}-c_{12}s_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta} &
    c_{12}c_{23}-s_{12}s_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta} & s_{23} c_{13}\\
    s_{12}s_{23}-c_{12}c_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta} &
   -c_{12}s_{23}-s_{12}c_{23}s_{13}e^{i\delta} & c_{23} c_{13}
  \epm \ ,
\ee
where $s_{ij}\equiv \sin \theta_{ij}$ and $c_{ij} \equiv \cos\theta_{ij}$ denote
the sine and cosine of the various mixing angles. Concerning the SM CKM matrix,
we have however traded the input parameters by the usual Wolfenstein parameters
$A$, $\lambda$, $\bar\rho$ and $\bar\eta$,
\be
  s_{12}^{\rm (CKM)} = \lambda \ , \qquad
  s_{23}^{\rm (CKM)} = A\lambda^2 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  s_{13}^{\rm (CKM)} e^{i\delta_{\rm CKM}} =
    \frac{A \lambda^3 \sqrt{1-A^2\lambda^4} (\bar\rho+i\bar\eta)}
      {\sqrt{1-\lambda^2} \big[1-A^2\lambda^4(\bar\rho+i\bar\eta)\big]} \ .
\ee

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.
3: 
4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18: 
19: from __future__ import annotations
20: 
21: import json
22: import re
23: import sys
24: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
25: from pathlib import Path
26: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
27: 
28: HEPTAPOD = Path.home() / "Documents/Github/heptapod"
29: SM_FR = HEPTAPOD / "tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr"
30: 
31: # Mathematica built-ins and FeynRules symbols a class, parameter or index must
32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}
39: 
40: # Names SM.fr declares: classes, class members, parameters, gauge groups, indices.
41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""
42: SM_CLASSES: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"ClassName\s*->\s*(\w+)", _SM_TEXT))
43: SM_MEMBERS: Set[str] = set()
44: for _m in re.findall(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", _SM_TEXT):
45:     SM_MEMBERS |= {x.strip() for x in _m.split(",") if x.strip()}
46: _i = _SM_TEXT.find("M$Parameters")
47: SM_PARAMS: Set[str] = set(re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\s*==\s*\{", _SM_TEXT[_i:], re.M)) if _i >= 0 else set()
48: SM_GAUGE = {"U1Y", "SU2L", "SU3C"}
49: SM_INDICES = {"Generation", "Colour", "Gluon", "SU2D", "SU2W", "Lorentz", "Spin",
50:               "Spin1", "Spin2", "Sextet"}
51: SM_FIELDS_ALL = SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS | {c + "bar" for c in SM_CLASSES | SM_MEMBERS}
52: SM_MASSES = {"MZ", "MW", "MH", "Me", "MMU", "MTA", "MU", "MC", "MT", "MD", "MS", "MB",
53:              "WZ", "WW", "WH", "WT"}
54: 
55: FR_BUILTINS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
56:                "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos",
57:                "Tan", "I", "Pi", "Sum", "Block", "Module", "ExpandIndices",
58:                "FlavorExpand", "True", "False", "bar", "anti", "left", "right",
59:                "Conjugate", "Re", "Im", "Abs", "Sig", "Ta", "T6", "K6", "K6bar",
60:                "K3", "K3bar", "f", "dSUN", "Dot", "Times", "Plus", "Power",
61:                "Automatic", "Internal", "External", "Unfold", "NoUnfold", "Range",
62:                "Index", "Lorentz", "Spin", "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation",
63:                "SU2D", "SU2W", "Sextet", "IndexStyle", "MakeIdenticalFermions",
64:                "Expand", "Simplify", "ProjPlus", "ProjMinus", "FR$", "vev"}
65: 
66: 
67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None
73: 
74: 
75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)
167:     term_names = {t["name"] for t in terms}
168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}
171:     for c in classes:
172:         cn = _prop(c["body"], "ClassName")
173:         if cn:
174:             class_names[cn] = c
175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:
177:                 class_idx[cn] = (mi.group(1), int(mi.group(2)))
178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------
182:     for name in list(class_names) + list(param_names) + list(index_decls):
183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:
184:             F.append(Finding("feynrules_symbol_name", "compile",
185:                              f"`{name}` is a FeynRules symbol", _line_of(text, name)))
186:         elif name in PROTECTED:
187:             F.append(Finding("protected_name", "warn",
188:                              f"`{name}` is a Mathematica built-in (loads with a warning; renaming is safer)",
189:                              _line_of(text, name)))
190:     for name in class_names:
191:         if name in SM_CLASSES or name in SM_MEMBERS:
192:             F.append(Finding("sm_class_redeclared", "warn",
193:                              f"class `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr (doubly-defined class)",
194:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {name}")))
195:     for name in param_names:
196:         if name in SM_PARAMS or name in SM_MASSES:
197:             F.append(Finding("sm_parameter_redeclared", "warn",
198:                              f"parameter `{name}` is already declared by SM.fr", _line_of(text, name)))
199:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
200:         for key in ("ParticleName", "AntiParticleName"):
201:             v = _prop(c["body"], key)
202:             names = re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', v) if v else []
203:             if v and any(re.search(r"[\'`\s!@#%^&*()=\[\]{}|\\;:<>?/,]", nm) for nm in names):
204:                 F.append(Finding("bad_particle_name", "mg5",
205:                                  f"class `{cn}`: {key} {v} is not a valid UFO identifier", _line_of(text, v)))
206:         if cn in class_idx and class_idx[cn][1] < 100:
207:             F.append(Finding("low_class_index", "warn",
208:                              f"class `{cn}` uses index {class_idx[cn][0]}[{class_idx[cn][1]}]; SM.fr uses the low indices",
209:                              _line_of(text, c["head"])))
210:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
211:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
212:                 if mem in SM_MEMBERS or mem in SM_CLASSES:
213:                     F.append(Finding("sm_member_redeclared", "compile",
214:                                      f"class member `{mem}` of `{cn}` collides with an SM.fr name",
215:                                      _line_of(text, mem)))
216:     if "$" in re.sub(r"M\$\w+", "", text):
217:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b\w*\$\w*", text):
218:             if not re.match(r"^(M|MR|FR)\$", m.group(0)):
219:                 F.append(Finding("dollar_in_name", "mg5", f"`{m.group(0)}` contains `$` (invalid Python)",
220:                                  text[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
221:                 break
222: 
223:     # --- rule 11: interaction orders --------------------------------------
224:     hierarchy = _block(text, "InteractionOrderHierarchy")
225:     orders_declared = set(re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*-?\d+\s*\}", hierarchy))
226:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
227:         body = p["body"]
228:         ptype = (_prop(body, "ParameterType") or "External").strip()
229:         io = _prop(body, "InteractionOrder")
230:         used = re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", term_bodies) is not None
231:         is_mass = any(re.search(rf"Mass\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"]) or
232:                       re.search(rf"Width\s*->\s*\{{\s*{re.escape(pn)}\b", c["body"])
233:                       for c in classes) or re.match(r"^(M|W)[A-Z]", pn) and not io
234:         if io:
235:             oname = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+)\s*,", io)
236:             for o in oname:
237:                 if o not in orders_declared and o not in ("QCD", "QED"):
238:                     F.append(Finding("order_not_in_hierarchy", "warn",
239:                                      f"parameter `{pn}` uses InteractionOrder `{o}` not listed in M$InteractionOrderHierarchy",
240:                                      _line_of(text, pn)))
241:     ordered = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items() if _prop(p["body"], "InteractionOrder")}
242:     internal = {pn for pn, p in param_names.items()
243:                 if (_prop(p["body"], "ParameterType") or "External").strip() == "Internal"}
244:     # an Internal parameter inherits the orders of the parameters in its Value
245:     for pn in list(internal):
246:         val = _prop(param_names[pn]["body"], "Value") or ""
247:         if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(o)}\b", val) for o in ordered):
248:             ordered.add(pn)
249:     for t in terms:
250:         if _is_kin_name(t["name"]):
251:             continue
252:         used_params = {pn for pn in param_names if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(pn)}\b", t["body"])}
253:         sm_couplings = {"ee", "gw", "gs", "g1", "yl", "yu", "yd", "lam", "CKM"}
254:         if used_params and not (used_params & ordered) and not \
255:                 any(re.search(rf"\b{c}\b", t["body"]) for c in sm_couplings) and \
256:                 not any(re.search(rf"\b(DC|FS)\[", t["body"]) for _ in [0]):
257:             F.append(Finding("missing_interaction_order", "mg5",
258:                              f"`{t['name']}`: none of its parameters ({', '.join(sorted(used_params))}) carries an InteractionOrder",
259:                              t["line"]))
260: 
261:     # --- rule 12: pattern rules on tensor parameters -----------------------
262:     for pn, p in param_names.items():
263:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:?->", p["body"]) or "_?NumericQ" in p["body"]:
264:             F.append(Finding("pattern_rule_definition", "mg5",
265:                              f"parameter `{pn}` uses a pattern rule in Definitions/Value; FeynRules exports it verbatim as a UFO name",
266:                              _line_of(text, pn)))
267:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
268:         d = _prop(c["body"], "Definitions") or ""
269:         if re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_[^\]]*\]\s*:>", d) and not re.search(r"\w+\[[^\]]*_\s*[,\]]", d):
270:             pass  # `X[mu_] :> ...` is the normal FeynRules idiom; leave it
271: 
272:     # --- rule 13: explicit indices ------------------------------------------
273:     for t in terms:
274:         b = t["body"]
275:         for m in re.finditer(r"DC\[\s*(\w+)\[([^\]]*)\]\s*,", b):
276:             fld = m.group(1)
277:             c = class_names.get(fld)
278:             idx = (_prop(c["body"], "Indices") or "") if c else ""
279:             if c and re.search(r"Colour|Sextet|Gluon|Octet|Col", idx):
280:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "compile",
281:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on `{fld}` with an explicit colour-type index", t["line"]))
282:             else:
283:                 F.append(Finding("explicit_index_in_dc", "warn",
284:                                  f"`{t['name']}`: covariant derivative on an explicitly indexed field `{fld}`", t["line"]))
285:             break
286:         if re.search(r"Index\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]\s*,\s*Index\[\s*Generation", b) or \
287:                 re.search(r"\w+\[\s*Generation\s*,\s*\w+\s*\]", b):
288:             F.append(Finding("nested_generation_index", "compile",
289:                              f"`{t['name']}`: nested generation index", t["line"]))
290:         m = re.search(r"\b(\w+)\[\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|ii\d?)\s*,\s*(ff\d?|gen\d?|jj\d?)\s*\]\s*\w+bar\[", b)
291:         if m and m.group(1) in param_names:
292:             F.append(Finding("explicit_flavour_sum", "mg5",
293:                              f"`{t['name']}`: flavour matrix `{m.group(1)}` with explicit generation indices instead of matrix form",
294:                              t["line"]))
295: 
296:     # --- rule 14: one declared total ---------------------------------------
297:     roots = []
298:     for t in terms:
299:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{t['name']}\b", u["body"]) for u in terms if u is not t):
300:             roots.append(t["name"])
301:     if terms and not roots:
302:         F.append(Finding("no_total_lagrangian", "harness", "no Lagrangian symbol is a root (circular or empty)", None))
303:     elif len(roots) > 1:
304:         F.append(Finding("ambiguous_total", "harness",
305:                          f"{len(roots)} root Lagrangian symbols: {', '.join(roots)}", None))
306:     elif roots and roots[0] not in ("LTotal", "LTot", "LFull", "LBSM", "LNP", "Lag", "LagTot"):
307:         F.append(Finding("total_not_named_ltotal", "warn", f"the single root is `{roots[0]}`, not LTotal", None))
308:     field_tokens = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | SM_FIELDS_ALL
309:     for c in classes:
310:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
311:             field_tokens |= {x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()}
312:     for t in terms:
313:         rhs = t["body"].split("=", 1)[-1]
314:         if re.search(r"\bL\w+\b", rhs) and any(re.search(rf"\b{u['name']}\b", rhs) for u in terms if u is not t):
315:             continue  # a sum of other terms
316:         if not any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(f)}\b", rhs) for f in field_tokens):
317:             F.append(Finding("fieldless_term", "mg5", f"`{t['name']}` contains no field", t["line"]))
318: 
319:     # --- rule 15: declarations -----------------------------------------------
320:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
321:         sc = (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip()
322:         qn = _prop(c["body"], "QuantumNumbers")
323:         if sc == "True" and qn and re.search(r"->\s*-?[1-9]", qn):
324:             F.append(Finding("selfconjugate_with_qn", "warn",
325:                              f"class `{cn}` is SelfConjugate and carries QuantumNumbers {qn}",
326:                              _line_of(text, f"ClassName -> {cn}")))
327:         if sc == "True" and _prop(c["body"], "AntiParticleName"):
328:             pass
329:     # Majorana mass normalisation
330:     for cn, c in class_names.items():
331:         if (_prop(c["body"], "SelfConjugate") or "").strip() == "True" and c["head"].startswith("F"):
332:             mm = re.search(r"Mass\s*->\s*\{\s*(\w+)", c["body"])
333:             if not mm:
334:                 continue
335:             M = mm.group(1)
336:             pat = re.compile(rf"(-?\s*(?:1/2|0\.5|\(1/2\))?\s*\*?\s*{M}\b[^;]{{0,40}}{cn}bar\s*\.\s*{cn}\b)")
337:             for t in terms:
338:                 for hit in pat.finditer(t["body"]):
339:                     if not re.search(r"1/2|0\.5", hit.group(1)):
340:                         F.append(Finding("majorana_mass_no_half", "checks",
341:                                          f"`{t['name']}`: Majorana mass term for `{cn}` without the 1/2",
342:                                          t["line"]))
343:     # undeclared symbols in terms (conservative: capitalised identifiers used as fields)
344:     declared = set(class_names) | {c + "bar" for c in class_names} | set(param_names) | \
345:         SM_FIELDS_ALL | SM_PARAMS | SM_MASSES | FR_BUILTINS | set(term_names) | set(index_decls) | \
346:         {"If", "Which", "Table", "KroneckerDelta", "Transpose", "Inverse", "ArcTan", "Sec", "Csc",
347:          "Cot", "Abs", "MatrixExp", "DiagonalMatrix", "IdentityMatrix", "Sum", "Product"}
348:     for c in classes:
349:         for key in ("Mass", "Width"):
350:             v = _prop(c["body"], key) or ""
351:             declared |= set(re.findall(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", v)) - {"Internal", "External", "Automatic"}
352:     for c in classes:
353:         for m in re.finditer(r"ClassMembers\s*->\s*\{([^}]*)\}", c["body"]):
354:             for mem in [x.strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",") if x.strip()]:
355:                 declared |= {mem, mem + "bar"}
356:         for m in re.finditer(r"Unphysical\s*->\s*True", c["body"]):
357:             pass
358:     for t in terms:
359:         b = re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', "", t["body"])
360:         locals_ = set()
361:         for m in re.finditer(r"(?:Block|Module)\[\s*\{([^}]*)\}", b):
362:             locals_ |= {x.strip().split("=")[0].strip() for x in m.group(1).split(",")}
363:         for m in re.finditer(r"\b([A-Za-z]\w*)\b", b):
364:             s = m.group(1)
365:             if s in declared or s in locals_ or s == t["name"] or len(s) < 2:
366:                 continue
367:             if re.match(r"^(mu|nu|rho|sig|la|lam|al|be|sp|ss|ii|jj|kk|ll|ff|gg|cc|aa|bb|tt|rr|xx|yy|zz)\d*$", s):
368:                 continue
369:             if s in ("ExpandIndices", "FlavorExpand", "Index", "Sqrt", "HC"):
370:                 continue
371:             if s[0].isupper() and re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(s)}\s*[\[.]", b):
372:                 F.append(Finding("undeclared_symbol", "warn",
373:                                  f"`{t['name']}` uses `{s}` which is neither declared here nor by SM.fr",
374:                                  t["line"]))
375:                 break
376: 
377:     # --- rule 9: non-fundamental colour representations -----------------------
378:     for iname, rng in index_decls.items():
379:         if re.search(r"Range\[\s*6\s*\]", rng) and "AddGaugeRepresentation" not in text:
380:             F.append(Finding("sextet_without_representation", "warn",

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

337:         reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)

357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")

362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),

## Objective
- Read `TASK.md` fully, then extract the complete new-physics content of the ALRM_general (ALRSM, arXiv:1911.12883) model into a `spec.json` (FeynRulesModel JSON, model_name `"ALRM_general_gen"`), run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate until schema OK and lints judged harmless.
- Final deliverable message: a self-audit table (each term's charges/sums, signs chosen, roots/fractions verified, lints judged harmless) plus one line with the last `./frgen` result.

## Important Details

Structured schema for a FeynRules ``.fr`` model file.

This is the shared representation produced by Lagrangian extraction and consumed
by the ``.fr`` generator (render.py). Design principle: STRUCTURE the regular,
error-prone blocks (M$Parameters, M$ClassesDescription, M$GaugeGroups,
M$Information, IndexRange) so an LLM never hand-writes their Mathematica syntax,
and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO
bookkeeping) as verbatim Mathematica strings.

All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
NumberStr = str


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"


class ParamType(str, Enum):
    External = "External"
    Internal = "Internal"


class SpinType(str, Enum):
    S = "S"  # scalar
    F = "F"  # fermion
    V = "V"  # vector
    U = "U"  # ghost
    T = "T"  # tensor
    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
    RW = "RW"


class RangeKind(str, Enum):
    Unfold = "Unfold"
    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
    Range = "Range"


class PropType(str, Enum):
    Sine = "Sine"
    Straight = "Straight"
    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
    Curly = "Curly"
    W = "W"
    C = "C"
    S = "S"
    D = "D"


class PropArrow(str, Enum):
    true = "True"
    false = "False"
    none = "None"
    forward = "Forward"


class ModelInfo(BaseModel):
    authors: List[str]
    version: str
    date: str
    institutions: List[str] = []
    emails: List[str] = []


class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):
    """A M$GaugeGroups entry. Omitted entirely by BSM add-on models."""

    name: str  # LHS symbol: U1Y, SU2L, SU3C
    abelian: bool
    gauge_boson: str
    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":
        if self.abelian and not self.charge:
            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")
        if not self.abelian and not self.structure_constant:
            raise ValueError(
                f"gauge group {self.name}: non-Abelian group needs structure_constant"
            )
        return self


class IndexDecl(BaseModel):
    name: str  # Colour, Generation, SU2W ...
    range_kind: RangeKind
    size: int  # Range[size]
    style_symbol: Optional[str] = None  # IndexStyle[name, style_symbol]


class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """A M$Parameters entry (LHS symbol of ``==``)."""

    name: str
    parameter_type: Optional[ParamType] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
    definitions: List[Rule] = []
    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None
    tex: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None
    # tensor-only flags
    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None

    @property
    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.indices)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":
        if self.is_tensor:
            if self.value is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
                )
            if self.order_block is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
                )
        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
        if len(exclusive) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
            )
        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
            )
        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:
            raise ValueError(
                f"parameter {self.name}: External params must be real "
                "(split into real/imag or make Internal)"
            )
        return self


class MassSpec(BaseModel):
    """Renders 0 | {sym} | {sym,val} | {sym,Internal} | {gen,{m1,v1},...}."""

    massless: bool = False  # -> literal 0
    sym: Optional[str] = None
    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # number | "Internal" | "Automatic" | None
    members: List[Tuple[str, Optional[NumberStr]]] = []  # multi-gen

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "MassSpec":
        if not self.massless and not self.sym:
            raise ValueError("MassSpec needs massless=True or a sym")
        return self


class ParticleClass(BaseModel):
    """A M$ClassesDescription entry, e.g. ``S[100] == {...}``."""

    spin_type: SpinType
    class_index: int  # the n in S[100]
    class_name: str
    self_conjugate: bool
    indices: List[str] = []  # -> Index[...] wrapped
    flavor_index: Optional[str] = None  # BARE name
    class_members: List[str] = []
    mass: Optional[MassSpec] = None
    width: Optional[MassSpec] = None
    quantum_numbers: Dict[str, NumberStr] = {}  # values are strings -> preserve -1/3
    pdg: Optional[Union[int, List[int]]] = None
    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None
    unphysical: bool = False
    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM Mathematica rule strings
    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
    weyl_components: List[str] = []
    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
    chirality: Optional[str] = None

    @property
    def class_label(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":
        if self.unphysical:
            if self.mass or self.pdg:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"
                )
            if not self.definitions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields require definitions"
                )
        if len(self.class_members) > 1:
            if not self.flavor_index:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: multi-member class needs flavor_index"
                )
            n = len(self.class_members)
            for lst in (
                self.pdg,
                self.particle_name,
                self.antiparticle_name,
                self.full_name,
            ):
                if isinstance(lst, list) and len(lst) != n:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"particle {self.class_name}: list length must equal "
                        f"member count ({n})"
                    )
        if self.spin_type == SpinType.U:
            if self.self_conjugate:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"particle {self.class_name}: ghosts must be self_conjugate=False"
                )
            if not self.ghost:
                raise ValueError(f"particle {self.class_name}: ghost needs ghost=<boson>")
        return self


class LagrangianTerm(BaseModel):
    name: str  # LHS symbol
    expression: str  # VERBATIM Mathematica RHS
    delayed: bool = False  # True -> ":=", False -> "="


def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
    if not text:
        return False
    return re.search(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9$]){re.escape(name)}(?![A-Za-z0-9$])", text) is not None


def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
    """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
    texts: List[str] = []
    if p.value:
        texts.append(p.value)
    for r in p.value_rules:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    for r in p.definitions:
        texts.append(r.rhs)
    blob = " ".join(texts)
    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}


def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.

    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
    dependency cycle.
    """
    names = {p.name for p in params}
    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}

    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
    emitted: set = set()
    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order

    while remaining:
        progressed = False
        still: List[str] = []
        for n in remaining:
            if deps[n] <= emitted:
                ordered.append(by_name[n])
                emitted.add(n)
                progressed = True
            else:
                still.append(n)
        remaining = still
        if not progressed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
            )
    return ordered


class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""

    model_name: str
    info: ModelInfo
    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")

        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
        builtin = {
            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
        }
        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
        }
        missing = used - declared
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
            )

        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
        return self

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.

74: \abstract{
75: We perform a consistent analysis of the 
76: alternative left-right
77: symmetric model emerging from $E_6$ grand unification. We include a large set of
78: theoretical and experimental constraints, with a particular emphasis on dark
79: matter observables and collider signals. We show that the exotic neutrino
80: inherent to this class of models, the scotino, is a viable candidate for dark
81: matter satisfying relic density and direct detection constraints. This has
82: strong implications on the scotino mass restricting it to lie in a narrow
83: window, as well as on the spectrum of Higgs bosons,  rendering it predictable,
84: with a few light scalar, pseudoscalar and charged states. Moreover, we also show
85: that the extra charged $W'$ gauge boson can be light, and investigate the most
86: promising signals 
87: at the future high-luminosity upgrade of the
88: LHC. Our findings show that the most optimistic cosmologically-favoured scenarios should be observable at $5\sigma$, whilst others could leave visible hints provided the background is under good control at the systematical level.

100: \section{Introduction}
101: \label{sec:intro}
102: The nature of dark matter and its interactions 
103: is one of the most
104: puzzling conceptual issues of the Standard Model of particle physics and points
105: clearly towards the existence of new physics. So far, the most popular
106: extensions of the Standard Model (SM) that contain natural dark matter (DM)
107: candidates have been either supersymmetric, so that $R$-parity conservation
108: enforces a stable supersymmetric state behaving as a weakly-interacting massive
109: particle (WIMP)~\cite{Arcadi:2017kky}, or featuring axion-like particles that
110: could additionally shed light on a potential solution to the strong $CP$
111: problem~\cite{Kawasaki:2013ae,Graham:2015ouw}. While experimental DM searches
112: are on-going and put stronger and stronger constraints on the phenomenological
113: viability of the models, several new {\it ad-hoc} mechanisms have been recently
114: designed  to supplement the SM with a DM candidate. In the latter, the observed properties of
115: DM~\cite{Aghanim:2018eyx} can be successfully reproduced by an appropriate
116: tuning of the particle masses and properties. For instance, new force carriers
117: could be introduced to mediate the interactions of the dark sector with the SM
118: one, as within the dark photon or vector portal models~\cite{Feldman:2006wd,
119: Izaguirre:2015yja,Curtin:2014cca,Essig:2013lka,Davoudiasl:2012ag}. Differently,
120: the connection between the dark and visible sector could be realised through
121: interactions with vector-like fermions~\cite{Toma:2013bka,Giacchino:2013bta,
122: Giacchino:2014moa,Ibarra:2014qma,Giacchino:2015hvk,Colucci:2018vxz}. Whilst
123: appealing from a phenomenological point of view by virtue of their simplicity,
124: such DM setups are however quite unnatural. In this work, we therefore go back
125: to natural dark matter models and focus on a less studied class of scenarios
126: that emerges from the grand unification of the SM gauge interactions.
127: 
128: Grand unification models based on the breaking of the exceptional group
129: $E_6$~\cite{Gursey:1975ki,Achiman:1978vg} have been popular for awhile, at the
130: beginning as a result of developments in string theories~\cite{Hewett:1988xc},
131: then later as generators of models with additional $U(1)$ symmetries~\cite{
132: Langacker:1998tc}. These so-called $U(1)'$ models arise from considering the
133: $SO(10)\times U(1)$ subgroup of $E_6$. However, the $E_6$ group has also an
134: $SU(3)\times SU(3)\times SU(3)$ subgroup. One of these $SU(3)$ remains unbroken
135: and is associated with the SM strong interaction group $SU(3)_c$, while the
136: two others further break into the $SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_H \times U(1)_X$ group
137: that embeds the $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ electroweak symmetry. In the so-called
138: left-right symmetric model (LRSM), that naturally accounts for non-vanishing
139: neutrino masses~\cite{Pati:1974yy,Mohapatra:1974gc,Senjanovic:1975rk,
140: Mohapatra:1977mj}, $SU(2)_H$ is identified with $SU(2)_R$ and
141: $U(1)_X$ with $U(1)_{B-L}$. In such a configuration, the right-handed SM
142: fermions and the right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$ are collected into $SU(2)_R$
143: doublets. The structure of the Higgs sector could however lead to non-acceptable
144: tree-level flavour-violating interactions that would conflict with the observed
145: properties of kaon and $B$-meson systems. Consequently, the $SU(2)_R \times
146: U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry has to be broken at a very high energy scale to
147: mass-suppress any potential flavour-violating effect. This additionally pushes
148: the masses of the extra Higgs and gauge bosons of the model to the high scale,
149: making them unlikely to detect at the LHC. Furthermore, in its minimal
150: incarnation, the LRSM lacks any viable DM candidate~\cite{Bahrami:2016has}.
151: 
152: It is nevertheless possible to associate the $SU(2)_H$ symmetry with a different
153: $SU(2)_{R'}$ group in which the assignments of the SM fermions into doublets
154: are different~\cite{Ma:1986we,Frank:2005rb}. This model is called the
155: alternative left-right symmetric model (ALRSM)~\cite{Babu:1987kp,Ma:2010us}. In
156: this case, the $SU(2)_{R'}$ partner of the right-handed up-quark $u_R$ is an
157: exotic down-type quark $d_R'$ (instead of the SM right-handed down-type quark
158: $d_R$), and the $SU(2)_{R'}$ partner of the right-handed charged lepton $e_R$ is
159: a new neutral lepton, the scotino $n_R$ (instead of the more standard
160: right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$). The right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$ and down-type
161: quark $d_R$ therefore remain singlets under both the $SU(2)_L$ and $SU(2)_{R'}$
162: groups. In addition, the model field content also includes $SU(2)_L$ singlet
163: counterparts to the new states, \ie\ an $n_L$ scotino and a $d_L'$ down-type
164: quark. Consequently, one generation of quarks is described by one $SU(2)_L$
165: doublet $Q_L = (u_L, d_L)$, one $SU(2)_{R'}$ doublet $Q_R = (u_R, d_R')$ and two
166: $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_{R'}$ singlets $d_L'$ and $d_R$. Similarly, one generation
167: of leptons is described by one $SU(2)_L$ doublet $L_L = (\nu_L, e_L)$, one
168: $SU(2)_{R'}$ doublet $L_R = (n_R, e_R)$ and two $SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_{R'}$
169: singlets $n_L$ and $\nu_R$. Moreover, the right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$ and the $n_L$
170: scotino being singlets under $U(1)_{B-L}$,  are unlikely to be
171: viable DM candidates, as their too weak interactions with the SM particles would
172: make them over-abundant. On the contrary, the $n_R$ scotino may fulfill the role.
173: 
174: In this work, we will show that this is indeed the case. The $n_R$ scotino can
175: be an acceptable DM candidate satisfying requirements from imposing agreement
176: with the observed relic density and the non-violation of the DM direct and indirect detection
177: bounds. This however yields very stringent constraints on the model parameter
178: space. In contrast with the usual LRSM, the charged right-handed gauge boson
179: $W'$ couples right-handed up-type quarks and charged leptons to their exotic
180: quarks and scotino partners. Therefore, the limits on the $W'$-boson mass
181: (originating mainly from the properties of the $K^0-{\bar K}^0$ mixing in the
182: LRSM case~\cite{Barenboim:1996nd}) do not apply. Similarly, the different
183: couplings of the Higgs states to fermions  forbid most dangerous
184: flavour-violating effects, so that the mass limits on the Higgs states can also
185: be relaxed. As will be demonstrated in the rest of this paper, these
186: considerations lead to a quite predictable lower-energy spectrum with signatures
187: potentially observable at the high-luminosity LHC.
188: 
189: The aim of this work is therefore to provide a comprehensive analysis of the
190: ALRSM setup, emphasising for the first time the complementarity between
191: cosmological, low-energy and collider constraints in this class of extensions of
192: the SM. We update and extent previous recent works that have focused on the dark
193: matter~\cite{Khalil:2010yt} and collider~\cite{Ashry:2013loa} phenomenology
194: independently. In section~\ref{sec:ALRSMmodel}, we provide a brief description
195: of the ALRSM and detail the technical setup underlying our analysis in
196:  section \ref{sec:scan}. Our results are presented in the next sections. In
197: section~\ref{sec:gaugebosons}, we analyse the constraints on the model parameter
198: space originating from LHC searches for new gauge bosons,  performed in a
199: similar way as for the LRSM~\cite{Frank:2018ifw}. Section~\ref{sec:dm}
200: is dedicated to cosmological considerations and their impact on the parameter
201: space. In section~\ref{sec:collider} we focus on determining promising
202: signals of the model at the future high-luminosity upgrade of the LHC. We
203: summarise our work and conclude in section~\ref{sec:conclusion}. In
204: appendices~\ref{app:higgs} and \ref{app:ferms}, we include further details on
205: the diagonalisation of the model Higgs and fermionic sector respectively, and
206: document our implementation of the ALRSM in \fr~\cite{Alloul:2013bka} in
207: appendix~\ref{app:fr}.

213: \section{The alternative left-right symmetric model}
214: \label{sec:ALRSMmodel}
215: The alternative left-right symmetric model~\cite{Ma:1986we,Babu:1987kp,
216: Frank:2005rb,Ma:2010us} is a variant of the more usual minimal left-right
217: symmetric model. It is based on the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times
218: SU(2)_{R'} \times U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge group, to which we supplement a global
219: $U(1)_S$ symmetry. The spontaneous breaking of $SU(2)_{R'}\times U(1)_S$ is
220: implemented so that the $L=S+T_{3R}$ charge, that can be seen as a generalised
221: lepton number, remains unbroken (with $T_{3R}$ being the third generator of
222: $SU(2)_{R'}$).
223: 
224: The quantum numbers and representations chosen for the fermionic field content
225: of the ALRSM are motivated by heterotic superstring models in which all SM
226: matter multiplets are collected into a ${\bf 27}$-plet of $E_6$.
227: Under the $E_6$ maximal subgroup $SU(3)_c \times SU(3)_L \times SU(3)_H$,
228: the ${\bf 27}$ representation is decomposed as
229: \be
230:   {\bf  27} =  \big({\bf 3}, {\bf 3}, 1\big) +
231:     \big({\bf \bar 3}, 1, {\bf \bar 3}\big) +
232:     \big(1, {\bf \bar 3}, {\bf 3}\big)
233:    \qquad \equiv \quad q \quad + \quad {\bar q} \quad + \quad l \ .
234: \ee
235: Explicitly, the particle content for this decomposition can be written, ignoring
236: the sign structure for clarity, as
237: \be\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.4}
238:   q        = \bpm u_L\\d_L\\d_L'\epm \ , \qquad
239:   {\bar q} = \bpm u_R^c & d^c_R & d_R^{\prime c}\epm \ , \qquad
240:   l = \bpm E_R^c&N_L&\nu_L\\ N_R^c&E_L&e_L\\ e_R^c&\nu_R^c&n_R^c\epm\ ,
241: \label{eq:331_fields}\ee
242: where $d'$, $E$, $N$ and $n$ are exotic fermions and $u$, $d$, $e$ and $\nu$ are
243: the usual up-type quarks, down-type quarks, charged leptons and neutrinos. In
244: this setup, $SU(3)_L$ operates vertically and $SU(3)_H$ horizontally. There are
245: three different ways to embed $SU(2)_H$ into $SU(3)_H$~\cite{Ma:1986we}. The
246: most common one consists in imposing the first and second column of the above
247: multiplets to form $SU(2)_H$ doublets, which corresponds to the usual LRSM
248: ($SU(2)_H = SU(2)_R$)~\cite{Pati:1974yy,Mohapatra:1974gc,Senjanovic:1975rk,
249: Mohapatra:1977mj}. The second option requires in contrast that the first
250: and third columns of the above multiplets form an $SU(2)_H$ doublet, which
251: corresponds to the ALRSM ($SU(2)_H = SU(2)_{R'}$)~\cite{Ma:1986we,Babu:1987kp,
252: Frank:2005rb,Ma:2010us} . Finally, the third and last option corresponds to
253: doublets formed from the second and third columns of the above multiplets, which
254: corresponds to the Inert Doublet Model ($SU(2)_H = SU(2)_I$)~\cite{
255: Deshpande:1977rw,Ma:2006km,Barbieri:2006dq}.
256: 
257: We are interested here in the
258: second option. In the rest of this section, we present a summary of the model
259: description, leaving computational details for the appendix. While previous
260: descriptions of the ALRSM exist, we provide extensive details to properly and
261: consistently define our notations, which is relevant for the model
262: implementation in the high-energy physics tools depicted in
263: section~\ref{sec:scan}.

305: 
306: Pairing the fields presented in eq.~\eqref{eq:331_fields} into $SU(3)_c \times
307: SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_{R'}\times U(1)_{B-L}$ multiplets yields phenomenological
308: issues for the neutrino sector, as the lightest neutrinos get
309: masses of the order of the up quark mass~\cite{Frank:2004vg}. This can be cured
310: by adding an $E_6$ singlet scotino
311: $n_L$ to the field content, together with a pair of (heavy) ${\bf 27} + {\bf
312: \overline{27}}$ Higgs fields. As a consequence, the exotic $E$ and $N$ fermions
313: become much heavier and can be phenomenologically ignored. The resulting
314: fermionic content of the model is presented in the left panel of
315: table~\ref{tab:content}, together with the representations under the model gauge
316: group and the associated $U(1)_S$ quantum numbers. The electric charge of the
317: different fields can be obtained through a generalised Gell-Mann-Nishijima
318: relation $Q = T_{3R} + T_{3L} + Y_{B-L}$, which subsequently explains the
319: unconventional $B-L$ charges.
320: 
321: In order to recover the electroweak symmetry group, the gauge and global
322: symmetry $SU(2)_{R'} \times U(1)_{B-L} \times U(1)_S$ is first broken down to
323: the hypercharge $U(1)_Y$ while preserving the generalised lepton number $L$.
324: This is achieved through an $SU(2)_{R'}$ doublet of scalar fields $\chi_R$
325: charged under $U(1)_S$. While we introduce an $SU(2)_L$ counterpart $\chi_L$ to
326: maintain the left-right symmetry, the latter is in contrast blind to the global
327: $U(1)_S$ symmetry. The electroweak symmetry is then broken down to
328: electromagnetism by means of a bidoublet of Higgs fields charged under both
329: $SU(2)_L$ and $SU(2)_{R'}$, but with no $B-L$ quantum numbers. We refer to the
330: right panel of table~\ref{tab:content} for details on the gauge and Higgs
331: sector of the ALRSM.
332: 
333: The model Lagrangian includes, on top of standard gauge-invariant kinetic terms
334: for all fields, a Yukawa interaction Lagrangian $\lag_{\rm Y}$ and a scalar
335: potential $V_{\rm H}$. The most general Yukawa Lagrangian allowed by the gauge
336: and the global $U(1)_S$ symmetries is given by
337: \be\label{eq:yuk}
338:   \lag_{\rm Y} = \bar Q_L {\bf \hat Y}^u \hat\phi^\dag Q_R
339:     - \bar Q_L {\bf \hat Y}^d \chi_L d_R
340:     - \bar Q_R {\bf \hat Y}^{d'}\chi_R d'_L
341:     - \bar L_L {\bf \hat Y}^e \phi L_R
342:     + \bar L_L {\bf \hat Y}^\nu \hat\chi_L^\dag \nu_R
343:     + \bar L_R {\bf \hat Y}^n \hat\chi_R^\dag n_L + {\rm h.c.} \ ,
344: \ee
345: where all flavour indices have been omitted for clarity so that the Yukawa
346: couplings ${\bf \hat Y}$ are $3 \times 3$ matrices in the flavour space,
347:  and where the hatted quantities refer to the duals of the scalar fields
348: $\hat\phi=\sigma_2\phi\sigma_2$ and $\hat\chi_{L,R}= i \sigma_2 \chi_{L,R}$ (with
349: $\sigma_2$ being the second Pauli matrix).
350: The most general Higgs potential $V_{\rm H}$ preserving the left-right symmetry
351: is given, following standard conventions~\cite{Borah:2010zq}, by
352: \be\bsp
353:   V_{\rm H} = &
354:    -\mu_1^2 {\rm Tr} \big[\phi^\dag \phi\big]
355:    -\mu_2^2 \big[\chi_L^\dag \chi_L + \chi_R^\dag \chi_R\big]
356:    + \lambda_1 \big({\rm Tr}\big[\phi^\dag \phi\big]\big)^2
357:    + \lambda_2\ (\phi\!\cdot\!\hat\phi)\ (\hat\phi^\dag\!\cdot\!\phi^\dag)
358: \\&
359:    + \lambda_3 \Big[\big(\chi_L^\dag \chi_L\big)^2 +
360:          \big(\chi_R^\dag\chi_R\big)^2\Big]
361:    + 2 \lambda_4\ \big(\chi_L^\dag \chi_L\big)\ \big(\chi_R^\dag\chi_R\big)
362:    + 2 \alpha_1 {\rm Tr} \big[\phi^\dag \phi\big]
363:           \big[\chi_L^\dag \chi_L + \chi_R^\dag \chi_R\big]
364: \\&
365:    + 2 \alpha_2 \big[ \big(\chi_L^\dag \phi\big) \big(\chi_L\phi^\dag\big) +
366:           \big(\phi^\dag \chi_R^\dag\big)\ \big(\phi\chi_R\big)\big]
367:    + 2 \alpha_3 \big[ \big(\chi_L^\dag \hat\phi^\dag\big)\
368:           \big(\chi_L\hat\phi\big) + \big(\hat\phi\chi_R^\dag\big)\
369:           \big(\hat\phi^\dag\chi_R\big)\big]
370: \\&
371:    + \kappa \big[\chi_L^\dag \phi \chi_R + \chi_R^\dag\phi^\dag\chi_L\big] \ ,
372: \esp\label{eq:Hpot}\ee
373: and contains bilinear ($\mu$), trilinear ($\kappa$) and quartic 
374: ($\lambda$, $\alpha$) contributions. In the above expression, the dot to the
375: $SU(2)$-invariant product.
376: 
377: After the breaking of the left-right symmetry down to electromagnetism, the
378: neutral components of the scalar fields acquire non-vanishing vacuum expectation
379: values (vevs),
380: \be
381:   \langle \phi  \rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bpm 0&0\\0 & k \epm\ , \qquad
382:   \langle \chi_L\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bpm 0\\ \vL \epm\ , \qquad
383:   \langle \chi_R\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bpm 0\\ \vR \epm\ ,
384: \label{eq:symbreak}\ee
385: with the exception of $\phi^0_1$, which is protected by the conservation of the
386: generalised lepton number that also forbids mixing between the SM $d$ and
387: exotic $d^\prime$ quarks.
388: 
389: Moreover, all scalar fields with the same electric
390: charge mix. Expressing the complex neutral scalar fields in terms of their real
391: degrees of freedom,
392: \be\bsp
393:  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
394:   \phi_1^0 =&\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
395:      \Big[ \Re\{\phi^0_1\} + i\ \Im\{\phi^0_1\}\Big]\ ,
396: \\
397:   \phi_2^0 =&\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
398:      \Big[ k + \Re\{\phi^0_2\} + i\ \Im\{\phi^0_2\}\Big] \ ,
399: \\
400:   \chi_{L,R}^0 =&\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
401:      \Big[ v_{\scriptscriptstyle L,R} + \Re\{\chi^0_{L,R}\} +
402:      i\ \Im\{\chi^0_{L,R}\}\Big]\ ,
403: \esp\ee
404: we can write the mixing relations involving the massive $CP$-even Higgs bosons
405: $H_i^0$ (with $i=0,1,2,3$), the massive $CP$-odd Higgs bosons $A_i^0$ (with
406: $i=1,2$) and the two massless Goldstone bosons $G_1^0$ and $G_2^0$ that give
407: rise to the longitudinal degrees of freedom of the $Z$ and $Z'$ bosons, as
408: \be
409:  \bpm \Im\{\phi_1^0\}\\\Im\{\phi_2^0\}\\\Im\{\chi_L^0\}\\\Im\{\chi_R^0\}\epm =
410:  \bpm 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0&&& \\ 0&& U_{3\times 3}^{\rm A} & \\0&&& \\ \epm
411:  \bpm A_1^0\\ G_1^0 \\ G_2^0\\A_2^0\epm \qquad\text{and} \qquad
412:  \bpm \Re\{\phi_1^0\}\\\Re\{\phi_2^0\}\\\Re\{\chi_L^0\}\\\Re\{\chi_R^0\}\epm =
413:  \bpm 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0&&& \\ 0&& U_{3\times 3}^{\rm H} & \\0&&& \\ \epm
414:   \bpm H_1^0\\ H_0^0 \\ H_2^0\\H_3^0\epm   \ .
415: \label{eq:nh_mix}\ee
416: The $\phi_1^0$ field has been prevented from any mixing by virtue of the
417: conservation of the generalised lepton number, and we refer to
418: appendix~\ref{app:higgs} for the expressions of the $3\times 3$ Higgs mixing
419: matrices $U_{3\times 3}^{\rm A}$ and $U_{3\times 3}^{\rm H}$, as
420: well as for those of the six Higgs-boson masses.
421: In the charged sector, the $\phi_1^\pm$, $\phi_2^\pm$, $\chi_L^\pm$ and
422: $\chi_R^\pm$ fields mix into two physical massive charged Higgs bosons $H_1^\pm$
423: and $H_2^\pm$, as well as  two massless Goldstone bosons $G_1^\pm$ and $G_2^\pm$
424: that are absorbed by the $W$ and $W'$ gauge bosons,
425: \be\bsp
426:  \bpm \phi_2^\pm\\\chi_L^\pm\epm =
427:  \bpm \cos\beta & \sin\beta\\ -\sin\beta & \cos\beta\epm
428:  \bpm H_1^\pm\\G_1^\pm\epm \ , \ \
429:  \bpm \phi_1^\pm\\\chi_R^\pm\epm =
430:  \bpm \cos\zeta & \sin\zeta\\ -\sin\zeta & \cos\zeta\epm
431:  \bpm H_2^\pm\\G_2^\pm\epm \ ,
432: \esp\label{eq:ch_mix}\ee
433: with
434: \be
435:   \tan\beta = \frac{k}{\vL} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \tan\zeta = \frac{k}{\vR} \ .
436: \ee
437: We refer again to appendix~\ref{app:higgs} for the explicit expressions of the masses of
438: the physical states in terms of other model parameters.
439: 
440: By definition, the breaking of the left-right symmetry generates masses for the
441: model gauge bosons and induces their mixing (from the Higgs-boson kinetic
442: terms). The charged $W=W_L$ and $W'=W_R$ bosons do not mix as $\langle\phi_1^0
443: \rangle = 0$, and their masses are given by
444: \be
445:   M_W    = \frac12 \gL \sqrt{k^2+\vL^2} \equiv \frac12 \gL v
446:  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
447:   M_{W'} = \frac12 \gR \sqrt{k^2+\vR^2} \equiv \frac12 \gR v' \ .
448: \label{eq:mw_mwp}\ee
449: In the neutral sector, the gauge boson squared mass matrix is written, in the
450: $(B_\mu, W_{L\mu}^3, W_{R\mu}^3)$ basis, as
451: \be
452:   ({\cal M}^0_V)^2 = \frac14 \bpm
453:     \gBL^2\ (\vL^2+\vR^2)  & -\gBL\ \gL\ \vL^2    & -\gBL\ \gR\ \vR^2\\
454:    -\gBL\ \gL\ \vL^2       &  \gL^2\ v^2          & -\gL\ \gR\ k^2\\
455:    -\gBL\ \gR\ \vR^2       & -\gL\ \gR\ k^2       &  \gR^2\ v^{\prime 2}
456:   \epm \ .
457: \ee
458: It can be diagonalised through three rotations that mix the $B$, $W_L^3$ and
459: $W_R^3$ bosons into the massless photon $A$ and massive $Z$ and $Z'$ states,
460: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.}
461: \be
462:   \bpm B_\mu\\ W_{L\mu}^3\\ W_{R\mu}^3\epm = 
463:   \bpm c_{\phw} & 0 & -s_{\phw}\\ 0 & 1 & 0\\ s_{\phw} & 0 & c_{\phw} \epm
464:   \bpm c_{\tw} & -s_{\tw} & 0\\ s_{\tw} & c_{\tw} & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 1 \epm
465:   \bpm 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & c_{\zw} & -s_{\zw}\\ 0 & s_{\zw} & c_{\zw} \epm
466:   \bpm A_\mu\\ Z_\mu\\ Z^\prime_\mu\epm  \ ,
467: \ee
468: where $s_i$ and $c_i$ respectively denote the sine and cosine of the angle $i$.
469: The $\phw$-rotation mixes the $B$ and $W_R^3$ bosons into the hypercharge boson
470: $B'$ as generated by the breaking of $SU(2)_{R'}\times U_{B-L}$ into to the
471: hypercharge group $U(1)_Y$. The $\tw$-rotation denotes the usual electroweak
472: mixing, and the $\zw$-rotation is related to the strongly constrained $Z$/$Z'$
473: mixing. The various mixing angles are defined by
474: \be\bsp
475:  & s_{\phw} = \frac{\gBL}{\sqrt{\gBL^2+\gR^2}} = \frac{\gY}{\gR}
476:    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
477:    s_{\tw}  = \frac{\gY}{\sqrt{\gL^2+\gY^2}} = \frac{e}{\gL} \ ,
478:  \\&
479:   \tan(2\zw)=\frac{2 c_{\phw} c_{\tw} \gL \gR (c_{\phw}^2 k^2-s_{\phw}^2\vL^2)}
480:      {-(\gL^2 - c_{\phw}^2 c_{\tw}^2 \gR^2) c_{\phw}^2 k^2 -
481:          (\gL^2 - c_{\tw}^2 \gBL^2 s_{\phw}^2) c_{\phw}^2 \vL^2 +
482:           c_{\tw}^2 \gR^2 \vR^2} \ ,
483: \esp\label{eq:ewmix}\ee
484: where $\gY$ and $e$ denote the hypercharge and electromagnetic coupling
485: constant respectively. Neglecting the $Z$/$Z'$ mixing, the $Z$ and $Z'$ boson
486: masses are given by
487: \be
488:   M_{Z} =  \frac{\gL}{2 c_{\tw}} \ v
489:   \qquad\text{and}\qquad
490:   M_{Z'} = \frac12 \sqrt{\gBL^2 s_{\phw}^2 \vL^2 +
491:      \frac{\gR^2 (c_{\phw}^4 k^2 + \vR^2)}{c_{\phw}^2}} \ .
492: \label{eq:mz_mzp}\ee
493: 
494: The breaking of the gauge symmetry furthermore generates masses and mixings in
495: the fermion sector. The masses of the up-type quark and charged leptons are
496: controlled by the vev $k$ of the Higgs bidoublet, whereas the masses of the
497: neutrinos and the down-type quarks arise from the vev $\vL$ of the $\chi_L$
498: Higgs triplet. The scale of the exotic fermion masses is in contrast solely
499: induced by the vev $\vR$ of the $\chi_R$ triplet. Similarly
500: to what is achieved in the LRSM, all fermion mixing are conveniently absorbed into
501: two CKM ($V_{\rm CKM}$ and $V_{\rm CKM'}$) and two PMNS ($V_{\rm PMNS}$ and
502: $V_{\rm PMNS'}$) rotations,
503: \be
504:   d_L  \to V_{\rm CKM} d_L \ , \quad
505:   \nu_L\to V_{\rm PMNS} d_L \ , \quad
506:   d'_R \to V_{\rm CKM'} d'_R\ , \quad
507:   n_R  \to V_{\rm PMNS'} n_R \ .
508: \ee
509: We refer to appendix~\ref{app:ferms} for additional details on the generation of
510: the fermion masses, and their explicit expression in terms of the other model
511: free parameters.
512: 
513: Finally, we supplement the model Lagrangian by the effective couplings
514: $a_{\rm H}^g$ and $a_{\rm H}^a$ of the SM Higgs boson to gluons and photons,
515: \be
516:  \lag_{\rm eff} = -\frac14 a_{\rm H}^g H_0^0 G_{\mu\nu}^a G^{\mu\nu}_a
517:    - \frac14 a_{\rm H}^a H_0^0 F_{\mu\nu} F^{\mu\nu} \ ,
518: \ee
519: where $G_{\mu\nu}^a$ and $F_{\mu\nu}$ respectively denote the gluon and photon
520: field strength tensors.
